key_insight: Learning and equilibrium computation are possible even when the learner only observes ordinal (ranking) feedback instead of numeric utilities: the paper provides algorithms that use ranking information to achieve provable online-learning guarantees and drive game dynamics toward equilibria in adversarial environments.
problem_solved: How to perform online learning and compute game-theoretic equilibria when the environment supplies only ranking/ordinal feedback (e.g., human preferences or privacy-restricted signals) rather than numeric rewards or utilities.
method: Formalize an online-learning model with ranking (ordinal) feedback and characterize the information limitation relative to numeric feedback.

Design learning algorithms that convert ranking signals into usable update directions via pairwise-comparison estimators and partial-information (bandit-like) updates, with provable regret bounds under adversarial conditions.

Use the online-learning procedures as no-regret dynamics to obtain convergence guarantees to approximate equilibria in games, establishing a bridge between ranking feedback and equilibrium computation.
impact: Provides practitioners a pathway to deploy online learning and equilibrium-seeking systems in settings where only preference rankings are available (e.g., human-in-the-loop systems, privacy-sensitive platforms), without sacrificing theoretical performance guarantees.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: numeric-reward pipeline vs. ranking-feedback pipeline showing where information is missing and how the algorithm compensates.
Flowchart of the algorithm: ranking input → pairwise estimators → update rule → regret bound / equilibrium output.
Performance plot: regret or convergence rate curves comparing ranking-feedback algorithm to a baseline with full numeric feedback (conceptual illustration).
Game diagram: small multi-player game showing repeated play under ranking feedback converging to an approximate equilibrium (icons for players and preference lists).
paper_title: Online Learning and Equilibrium Computation with Ranking Feedback
paper_authors: Mingyang Liu, Yongshan Chen, Zhiyuan Fan, Gabriele Farina, Asuman Ozdaglar
